target_questions.question: Is ligament formation and shedding a recurrent process, and what controls successive events?
target_questions.target_basis: Tier 1 C007 identifies a wave-to-ligament cascade; this combined experiment/DNS resolves the ligament step directly.

evidence_candidates.claim_text: Validated three-dimensional simulations and experiments show recurrent ligament formation after liquid-sheet rupture; the first shedding is weakly Weber-dependent, while later shedding is driven mainly by inertia and wake-vortex dynamics.
evidence_candidates.evidence_summary: Fourier decomposition identifies azimuthal modes that destabilize the sheet and repeated shedding events.

core_links.shared_parameter_or_mechanism: wave cascade terminates through ligament-mediated fragmentation

limitations: Water-droplet aerobreakup in the studied high-speed regime; later fragment statistics remain outside the claim.
visual_verification: Targeted visual verification performed where numeric/glyph-dependent abstract claims required it; no figure digitization.
